reasoning: The question asks whether the 4-week secondary market treasury bill rate will increase between March 15 and March 22, 2026. The evidence shows recent 4-week bill yields from January (3.595% on Jan 15, 3.630% on Jan 22) and 3-month bill yields rising to 3.610% on March 2. The Fed held rates steady in January and is scheduled to meet March 17-18, with most economists forecasting two rate cuts in 2026 (likely June or later). Short-term treasury yields have shown modest upward pressure in early 2026, but the upcoming FOMC meeting on March 17-18 creates uncertainty. A one-week forecast for a specific directional move in short-term rates is inherently uncertain. Given the recent modest upward trend in short-term yields, the proximity to an FOMC meeting, and the lack of specific data for mid-to-late March, the probability of an increase over this narrow 7-day window is slightly below 50%, as short-term rates are volatile and could move either direction.
